clue.text: Let slip bowl at first test venue

indicators.note: at first asks for only the opening letter of the word bowl

parts.note: a lab, or laboratory, is where tests are carried out

explanation.surface: A cricket report on a test ground where the first ball was bowled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Test venue' suggests a cricket ground, but here it is a laboratory.
explanation.definitionFit: To blab is to reveal a secret through careless talk.

clue.text: Stir tea when talking? That's funny!

indicators.note: when talking says the word for tea is to be heard spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: a brew is a pot or cup of tea in British slang
ha-ha is what one says at something funny

explanation.surface: Someone stirring their tea while chatting finds something amusing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stir' looks like an instruction for the tea, but it is the definition, a commotion. BREW is British slang for tea.
explanation.definitionFit: A brouhaha is a noisy fuss or commotion, as is a stir.

clue.text: Spent nothing on Tyneside comprehensive?

parts.note: all in means exhausted, completely spent
O, the figure zero, stands for nothing
Tyneside is in the North East of England, abbreviated NE

explanation.surface: Someone from Newcastle who spent nothing at the local comprehensive school.
explanation.walkthrough: A comprehensive is a British state secondary school, which the surface plays on; the question mark flags that the word is really the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Something all-in-one covers everything in a single package, so it is comprehensive.

clue.text: Amount drunk by lady adjusted to satisfy

indicators.note: drunk by means swallowed inside, so one piece goes into the middle of the other
adjusted means the letters of lady are rearranged

parts.note: to amount to something is to equate to it

explanation.surface: A measure of drink taken by a woman, tweaked until it is enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk by' reads as drinking, but it signals one piece swallowed inside another; 'adjusted' turns the letters of 'lady' into ADLY. 'to satisfy' works adverbially: done well enough to satisfy.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something adequately means doing it well enough to meet requirements.

clue.text: Part below stamp displaying Spanish name

indicators.note: below, in a down answer, puts the second piece underneath the first

parts.note: a die is a tool that stamps a design onto metal
to part is to go away, depart

explanation.surface: Describes the lower section of a postage stamp showing a Spanish name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part' and 'stamp' look like nouns from philately; both are used in other senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Diego is a common Spanish given name, as in the painter Diego Velázquez.

clue.text: Dance record covered by Fleet Street

indicators.note: covered by, in a down answer, places the record beneath what comes before

parts.note: fleet as an adjective means swift or quick
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A dance record reviewed by the London newspaper world.
explanation.walkthrough: Fleet Street is the London street long home to British newspapers, so 'covered' reads as press coverage.
explanation.definitionFit: The quickstep is a fast ballroom dance.

clue.text: Feature in Paris Match re period fashions

indicators.note: fashions is a verb here, meaning shapes or reworks the preceding letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A French magazine article about clothes styles from a certain era.
explanation.walkthrough: Paris Match is a French weekly magazine, which makes 'Paris Match' look like a unit; 'Paris' belongs with the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The triumphal arch at the top of the Champs-Élysées is one of the landmarks of that city.

clue.text: Book flight

definitions.meaning: the second book of the Old Testament
a mass departure or fleeing of people

explanation.definitionFit: It names the Bible book telling of the Israelites leaving Egypt, and also any mass departure.

clue.text: Line in poem handled by younger type of singer

indicators.note: handled by means held between the two letters of the outer piece

parts.note: yr is a dictionary abbreviation for younger

indicators.note: in says the line goes inside the poem

parts.note: an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: A line in a poem recited by a youngster.
explanation.walkthrough: L inside ODE gives ODLE, and 'handled by' puts that between Y and R.
explanation.definitionFit: A yodeller sings with rapid switches between chest voice and falsetto, an Alpine style.

clue.text: Sloping past student, speaker's to escape

parts.note: OB, old boy, is a former pupil of a school

indicators.note: speaker's signals that the word for escape is to be heard, not written

parts.note: a leak is an escape of gas or liquid

explanation.surface: A former student on a slope trying to avoid a speech.
explanation.walkthrough: LIQUE is the spelling heard as 'leak', a gas escape.
explanation.definitionFit: Oblique means slanting, at an angle rather than straight.

clue.text: Question during Question Time is raised over Mass on a Sunday

indicators.note: over, in a down answer, puts the reversed piece above the next
on, in a down answer, puts the next piece below

parts.note: Qu again abbreviates question
during means in, as in the course of
Qu again abbreviates question
an age is a period of time

indicators.note: raised in a down answer means the letters of is are read upwards

parts.note: M is the symbol for mass in physics

explanation.surface: A query raised during a televised debate show about church services.
explanation.walkthrough: Question Time is a BBC political debate programme, which the surface leans on.
explanation.definitionFit: Quinquagesima is the Sunday before Lent begins, about fifty days before Easter.

clue.text: One new jam set with it

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a jam of people is a crowd

explanation.surface: A recipe note: a fresh jam has set properly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jam' and 'set' suggest preserves; 'with it' means fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: The in-crowd is the fashionable clique, a group of trendy people.

clue.text: In dark, confused with how one's doing

indicators.note: confused means the letters of the preceding words are jumbled together

explanation.surface: Someone fumbling in the dark, unsure how things are going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'how one's doing' reads as a greeting, but 'one's doing' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: One's handiwork is what one has done or made oneself.

clue.text: Former partner revealing all has no name to give out

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse or lover

indicators.note: has no says the letter for name is taken away from the word before

parts.note: someone nude has everything on show

explanation.surface: A former lover's tell-all story leaves out names.
explanation.walkthrough: NUDE without its N is UDE.
explanation.definitionFit: To exude is to discharge or emit, as a plant oozes sap.

clue.text: Hams and quantity of drink placed in hampers

indicators.note: placed in means put inside the word that follows

parts.note: hampers as a verb means hinders
a quart is a measure of liquid, two pints

explanation.surface: Picnic hampers packed with hams and bottles of drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hampers' looks like picnic baskets, but it is the verb, and 'Hams' are thighs and buttocks.
explanation.definitionFit: The hindquarters are the rear legs and rump, which hams are.

clue.text: Tea leaf proof that fine tea initially drunk

indicators.note: drunk suggests something reeling, so the letters are mixed up
initially takes only the opening letter of tea

explanation.surface: A claim that fine tea was consumed.
explanation.walkthrough: Tea leaf is Cockney rhyming slang for thief, so 'tea leaf proof' means thief-proof; 'drunk' rearranges THATFINE into ANTITHEF, before the T from 'tea initially'.
explanation.definitionFit: Anti-theft devices protect against robbers, making things thief-proof.

clue.text: Chuck is cracking black heavyweight

parts.note: jet is a deep glossy black

indicators.note: cracking means breaking into, so is goes inside the next piece

parts.note: a ton is a very heavy weight

explanation.surface: Someone called Chuck breaking into a black heavyweight boxer's defence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chuck' looks like a name, but it is the verb, to throw away.
explanation.definitionFit: To jettison is to throw overboard or discard, which is to chuck.

clue.text: Elevated ploy that is not heartless but greedy

indicators.note: elevated in a down answer means the word for ploy is read upwards

parts.note: a ruse is a ploy or trick
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

indicators.note: heartless removes the middle letter, keeping first and last

explanation.surface: A lofty scheme that is generous on the face of it but really grasping.
explanation.walkthrough: RUSE upwards gives ESUR; NOT without its middle O is NT.
explanation.definitionFit: Esurient is a literary word for hungry or greedy.

clue.text: Do spoilers work in story paper ruined?

indicators.note: in places the word for work inside the rearranged letters
ruined means the letters of story paper are wrecked and rearranged

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A newspaper article whose plot is given away, ruining it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do' is the noun, a party, so 'Do spoilers' are people who spoil a party; STORYPAPER rearranges to PARTYPOERS, with OP inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Party poopers are killjoys who dampen a celebration.

clue.text: Jersey maybe for child when city centre reaches zero Celsius

indicators.note: the centre of the city word reaches a new value, so its middle pair is swapped out

parts.note: Moscow is the capital city of Russia
O looks like the figure zero

explanation.surface: When the city centre drops to freezing point, zero degrees Celsius.
explanation.walkthrough: Jersey is a breed of dairy cow, not a garment; the middle letters SC of MOSCOW become OC.
explanation.definitionFit: Moo-cow is a nursery word for a cow, and a Jersey is one breed.

clue.text: Prayer has Psalms turn and turn about

indicators.note: about means around, so the turning word goes round the other

parts.note: to veer is to turn or change course

indicators.note: turn means the letters for Psalms are turned backwards

parts.note: Ps is the abbreviation for the book of Psalms

explanation.surface: A prayer that includes psalms read in turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' appears twice: the first reverses PS to SP, the second is VEER.
explanation.definitionFit: Vespers are evening prayers, and a vesper is one such evening service.

clue.text: Honours even in opening round

parts.note: OBEs, Orders of the British Empire, are honours

indicators.note: opening takes only the first letter of even

explanation.surface: Honours shared evenly in the first round of a contest.
explanation.walkthrough: An OBE is a British honour; 'round' is the adjective, plump.
explanation.definitionFit: Obese means very fat, as someone round in shape is.

clue.text: Head off to practise guitar with great Russian musician

indicators.note: head off says the first letter of the word is removed

parts.note: to strum is to play a guitar casually
Peter the Great was Tsar of Russia

explanation.surface: Someone sets off to practise guitar with a great Russian musician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head off' looks like 'set off', but it removes S from STRUM.
explanation.definitionFit: A trumpeter is a player of a brass instrument, a kind of musician.

clue.text: In France, a present lifted is not earned

parts.note: un is French for a

indicators.note: lifted in a down answer means the word for present is read upwards

parts.note: now means the present time

explanation.surface: A gift picked up in France that was not deserved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'present' looks like a gift but means the current moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unwon was not gained or achieved.

clue.text: Upset, bighead'll have a large one!

definitions.meaning: someone with a big head needs a big hat measurement

explanation.definitionFit: To overturn a boat is to tip it over, and a large head takes a large hat measurement.

clue.text: I'm poor person whose aims I meet regularly

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter, starting with the first

explanation.surface: A pauper laments the ambitions they meet along the way.
explanation.definitionFit: Woe is me is a lament, roughly 'poor me'.

clue.text: Justifying fighting without soldier, say

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the fighting word surrounds the other

parts.note: warring means fighting
a soldier is one kind of ant

explanation.surface: Justifying a war without any troops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but means outside; 'soldier, say' is an example of an ant.
explanation.definitionFit: Warranting means giving grounds for, which is justifying.

clue.text: Wrinkle reflecting fright in koala bears

indicators.note: reflecting means the letters are read backwards as in a mirror
bears means carries within, so the letters are concealed inside the words

explanation.surface: Koalas showing fear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bears' looks like the animals but means carries; the run TINK inside 'fright in koala' is read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To knit one's brows is to wrinkle them in a frown.
